Valeria Ryzhova has dreamed of being a ballerina for as long as she can remember. When she was nine, she could already perform flawless battements and cabriolet, albeit at the cost of a broken chandelier or two. After graduating from the Moscow Ballet Academy with honors, she was recruited to the Maya Plisetskaya Theater, where she very quickly became the most sought-after dancer. However, following the appearance of robot dancers, her popularity gradually began to wane. Deeply conflicted, she eventually came out against performances that included both human and robot ballerinas. No one took her position particularly seriously, since Ryzhova was known for being difficult, and the theater's staff had already grown accustomed to her flights of fancy. "You've cried wolf too many times!" Artistic Director Stefan Lastochkin once told his protégée.

Despite his parents' and teachers' expectations, Petelka did not become a famous physicist. Although he certainly had the potential, the young man's exceptional mind and fantastic imagination ultimately allowed his reach to exceed his grasp. Comrade Petelka learned about robots from a newspaper article even before the war and never stopped fantasizing about them. Petelka did end up becoming a physicist, although he was never famous. He worked with Comrade Filimonenko on a cold Polymer synthesis project, was an excellent robot configuration technician at the Maya Plisetskaya Theater, and even made his way to the secret departments of the AoC, where he truly felt his "insignificance before the vastness of the cosmos."  "I understand this world perfectly. We're all just grains of sand in an ocean of electrical connections," Comrade Petelka declared before retiring from science, effective immediately. But he did not leave the Facility. Having returned to his duties configuring robots and servicing the theater's electrical grid, Petelka is, perhaps more than any other Soviet citizen, eagerly anticipating the Kollektiv 2,0 update that will utterly efface the boundary between human cognition and the capabilities of robots.  "We're all just electric currents, just ones and zeroes" is a favorite phrase of Petelka's, who often spends his free time in the theater's coat check room observing his favorite robot, the coat check girl.

A top-notch neurosurgeon and colleague of Zakharov's, Dr. Filatova is a talented Academy employee and a specialist known for her intelligence and subtly manipulative behavior. After her mentor's death, she continued to work on integrating human consciousness into the Kollektiv 2.0 network. Her social rating has been reduced due to her romantic relationship with Viktor Petrov.

As a child in the hot city of Koktebel, Alexei Kasitsyn quickly developed a passion for the work of Russian botanist Ivan Michurin, even breeding an enormous ear of corn to the delight of his compatriots. His amazing creation can still be observed at the Facility 3826 VDNH today. After being awarded a medal of honor by Comrade Khrushchev, Junior Lab Assistant Kasitsyn took a brief vacation and returned to his hometown before taking charge of a new secret project in a more senior role.
